## Appeal Letter

Dear CareFirst Alliance,

I am writing to appeal the denial of claim #CLM-2024-03512 for CPT 90837 (Psychotherapy, 60 min) dated May 2, 2024. [S1]

The denial cites that mental health services are not a covered benefit under the plan. However, under the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA), group health plans that provide mental health or substance use disorder benefits must provide them on terms no more restrictive than medical/surgical benefits. [S2]

We request a copy of the plan's benefit determination criteria for mental health services and ask that the claim be reconsidered under parity standards.

Sincerely,
Sarah Williams

summary.explanation: Your mental health therapy claim was denied as a non-covered benefit. The insurer claims psychotherapy is excluded from your plan. However, the Mental Health Parity Act requires that if the plan covers any mental health benefits, it cannot impose more restrictive terms than medical/surgical coverage. This case requires human review because the specific plan language is ambiguous about the scope of mental health exclusions.

rule_sources.text: Group health plans that provide mental health or substance use disorder benefits may not apply financial requirements or treatment limitations to such benefits that are more restrictive than those applicable to medical and surgical benefits.

items.description: Request a copy of the plan's mental health benefit summary and exclusion list
items.rationale: Needed to determine whether MHPAEA applies or whether the exclusion is a true carve-out

items.description: Compare mental health visit limits against analogous medical/surgical visit limits in the plan
items.rationale: MHPAEA parity analysis requires a comparator benefit

items.description: Treating therapist's letter documenting medical necessity of ongoing psychotherapy
items.rationale: Strengthens the case if the denial is reclassified as medical necessity

success_estimate.explanation: Not-covered-benefit denials are the hardest to appeal unless a federal parity law applies. The MHPAEA argument has merit but requires detailed plan document analysis. Human review is recommended before submitting.
